newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech AgMin sees small flood impact on food prices.
newsitem.headline: Czech AgMin sees small flood impact on food prices.

text.p: Czech food prices should not be significantly pressured by this week's massive floods as there was enough commodities to supply the domestic market, the local news agency CTK quoted Agriculture Minister Josef Lux as saying on Thursday.

"I am not expecting any dramatic impact (of the floods) into the prices of agricultural production because we are in a situation with most commodities when we can sufficiently supply the domestic market," it quoted Lux as saying.
Lux said that he considered it "premature and useless" to attempt to estimate damages from the floods which have forced tens of thousands out of their homes and killed at least 17 people.
Some economists have taken rough estimates at the total damage to the economy ranging from 10 to 50 billion crowns.
The flood-affected areas grow wheat and other grains, rapeseed, sugar beet and potatoes.
Low-lying areas throughout the eastern quarter of the country have suffered from the floods described as worst this century after torrential rains continued from Saturday through Wednesday.
Parts of the city of Ostrava and town of Olomouc were flooded as well as scores of other towns and villages, but waters began receding in many areas.
Thousands of soldiers, firemen and rescuers continued evacuations as the flood wave moved south down the Morava river toward south-western Slovakia.
Parts of Poland and Austria have been affected as well. --Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
